newsitem.title: NIGER: World Bank to lend Niger $40 mln for health.
newsitem.headline: World Bank to lend Niger $40 mln for health.

text.p: The World Bank is to lend Niger 20 billion CFA francs ($40 million) to help the poor and arid West African nation improve its health care, a bank official said on Saturday.
Theodore Ahler, operations director for Niger, Benin and Togo, said a mission from the Bank would visit Niger in October to discuss a structural adjustment programme.
"The Bank will continue to support the efforts of Niger, with relations remaining strictly economic," Ahler told a news conference.

Military leader Ibrahim Bare Mainassara was elected Niger's president in July but was criticised by the United States for scrapping the independent electoral commission before the end of polling. Parliamentary elections are planned for November 10.
In June the International Monetary Fund granted Niger an Enhanced Structural Adjustment Facility loan after a five-year break in cooperation.
The Bank and Niger have about 10 projects in the health, education and farming. On the health front, Niger is particularly prey to meningitis.
